etymological_assessment: Ushojo wajuth body is segmentally consistent with regional wujūd-type body/existence vocabulary, not tanū or ḍimba. The exact contact route requires a primary regional source, so this remains a loan candidate rather than a claimed new inherited etymology.

research_link_evidence: Brokskat ṣiṣ and Ushojo ṣuṣ head preserve the sibilant frame of śīrṣá and directly match the short Shinaic head set. Shortening removes the long-vowel mora contrast; absent marks are not tonelessness.
Ushojo baale hair matches vā́la and Shina baal, with a final e cell and initial stress. The ending must be identified before using it as an unextended noun comparison.
Ushojo mukh face directly matches múkha; the related múkhya10174 is an alternative derivation but not independently needed for the exact segmental form.

Brokskat ac̣hii and Ushojo ɛṣiː eye match ákṣi/akṣī́ in the affricate cluster outcome and final i. Ushojo initial stress contrasts with final-vowel prominence in the other source; the singular/dual-derived input is deliberately left unresolved.

Brokskat kani ear has an extra final i and final stress; Ushojo koon is a contracted monosyllable. Both share the diagnostic k/n ear stem of kárṇa, but the Brokskat ending must be identified before calling its stress an unexplained shift.

Brokskat nuto and Ushojo noti nose preserve the n/t frame of nasta with gender/final-vowel differences. Both have initial syllable stress; vowel quantity and the o/i cell distinction must remain separate.
Ushojo doon teeth matches dánta with nt simplification and loss of final vowel, with a long rounded nucleus. It is a plural gloss but the actual cell is unspecified; no accent is marked.

Brokskat gip and Ushojo jib tongue match jihvā through contraction and labial stop outcome, with palatal onset spelled g/j. The final voicing difference remains recorded; neither token has a usable accent mark.

etymological_assessment: Ushojo buxthian breast has final stress and substantial derivative material. A vákṣas chest comparison is worth examining, but xth and ian must be explained; no link is accepted from anatomy alone.

research_link_evidence: Ushojo ḍɛṛ belly closely matches Shina ḍeer and the independently reconstructed ḍhiḍḍha belly family, including retroflexes and medial-cluster reduction.

Brokskat hat and Ushojo hʌt hand preserve h/t of hásta after cluster simplification. Both are short unmarked monosyllables, so they are segmental controls but have no observed early/late mora contrast.

etymological_assessment: Ushojo ṭhuuri elbow does not directly match kaphōṇi or mūṣala; compare limb/joint nouns independently and retain the observed initial stress.

research_link_evidence: Ushojo tale palm matches tala flat surface/palm with final e and initial stress, independently distinct from the Kalkoti sthavira-derived hand term.

Ushojo aŋguuli finger preserves aṅguli's nasal-velar/li structure and accents the medial syllable. Quantity differs from the short old u headword and must be distinguished from the *aṅgūḍi alternative.
Ushojo nokh fingernail retains the kh of nakhá rather than the r derivative nakhara. This independent segmental distinction selects the simpler input family without consulting accent.

etymological_assessment: Ushojo mootha(a)ro mirror may contain face/mouth plus a seeing or holding element, but neither compound structure nor source is secure. Final/medial stress is recorded without constructing a Sanskrit ancestor from the English meaning.
